page.layout: One page of running text in one column; marginal notes in the right margin: "Physica." beside line 1 of ¶1, "Medicina." beside ¶2, "Ethica-" beside ¶3.

main_text.p: tum singularum partiū tractant; quas quidem ratio vel simpliciter & per se considerat, vel ad hominum salutem & valetudinem simul refert: alię ad vitam rectè instituendam & mores pertinent.

1 Naturam totius universi seu mundi, & Physica. omnium ejus partiū simpliciter & per se contemplatur Physica, seu Physiologia, quæ causas & effectus quærit: de qua Plato in Timęo, Arist. in phys. in libr. de cœlo & mundo, de animal. & part.animal. & aliis; Et Cicero in particula Academic. Quæst. seu de philosophia; & de natura deor. l.2. & in libr. de universit. de qua verissimè Genes. tribus primis capitib. & Iobi aliquot ultimis, & in multis Psalmis. Nam ita cœli tandem enarrant gloriam Dei.

2 Res naturales illas omnes ad hominum Medicina. salutem & valetudinem refert Medicina, seu Iatrica: cùm nimirum Deus voluisset homini servire. Ita enim medicina sequitur physicam: de qua Hippo-crates, Galenus & alii.

3 Sed mores & vitam hominum quæ spe-Ethica-ctat,est Ethica, & ita de virtutib. ac vitiis,item de fine bonorum & malorum disserit accuratius: de qua Plato passim, quòd hanc Socrates inpri-mis coluisset,tum Xenophon in libris de dictis & factis Socratis, tum Aristoteles in Ethicis ad Nicomachum & Eudemum, & in illis Ethicis, quæ Magna vocat: de qua & Cicero in officiis, in libris de Finib. bonorum & malorum, in Tuscul. Quæstion. In paradoxis, & sæpe alibi: de qua passim in Bibliis, ut cùm Prophetæ & Apostoli

page.notes: The long s is written as plain s throughout. Macrons on "partiū" and "universi" are as printed. The hyphen in "Hippo-crates" and "inpri-mis" is a printed line-end hyphen. The signature "T 3" is at the foot of the page. The page is a continuing text page with no catchword. The word "universi" is printed "univerfi" and "Quæst." is printed "Quaest.", both transcribed with the long s normalised.
